title: Dead hang guide
summary: NH presents dead hangs as a weighted stretch for forearms, lats and arms that also aids injury prevention by decompressing the spine and relieving shoulders. He recommends doing them at the end of workouts three times a week (heavy, medium, light), warns about stretch-related tears and grip interference, and explains bracing abs and glutes to avoid lower back and SI joint spasms.
claims: Dead hangs are a convenient timed grip-strength test, but bodyweight changes affect the result
Grip strength matters to bodybuilders for hypertrophy-related reasons, not for testing strength
Holding a barbell trains the forearms but is not the best way to build big forearms
A dead hang gives the forearms a more intense stretch than holding a barbell because the shoulders are fully flexed and you hang with arms extended
The good-feeling stretch of a hang is really a weighted stretch of the lats, back and arms under load, which drives hypertrophy
Use at least a shoulder-width grip; narrower puts too much on the arms and the stretch can become dangerous
Supinated grip stretches the biceps most, neutral the triceps, pronated the lats, though all get some stimulus
Loaded-stretch movements are very valuable but dangerous: people have torn triceps and biceps (supinated) hanging; pronated is the least risky
Never jump into a hang; lower yourself slowly, and always be warmed up first
For hypertrophy do hangs at the end of the workout: you are warm, the fatigued grip raises the intensity, and it saves time; not for people chasing a fresh record
Hanging at the end of a session decompresses the spine after squats or deadlifts and relieves shoulder pain from pressing and front delt work
He hangs three times a week: a heavy day to failure, a medium day stopping at half his max time, and a light day of 10-30 seconds
Hanging every day is overkill; twice a week heavy and medium is enough

Muscles stretched in a hang are weakened afterward; e.g. skull crushers followed by neutral-grip hangs heavily stresses the triceps long head, which is why he likes body part splits that track where tonnage went
Avoid intense hangs before sessions that need grip; he never uses straps on curls and grip limits reps
Hanging fully relaxed with loose abs and glutes can trigger lower back and SI joint spasms because the pelvis never normally supports the legs; it happened to him and went away in a few days
Hang with abs braced and glutes engaged; if shoulders get uncomfortable, adjust torso angle and re-engage the lats
Hangs are a good way to improve overhead shoulder mobility for lockouts
Focusing on the stretch, glutes, abs and lats instead of the grip burn keeps your mind busy and lets you hang longer
Hangs are not time consuming; do them two or three times a week since too often is counterproductive, and experiment with grips and implements like fat grips or towels
exercises: at least shoulder-width grip; lower in slowly, never jump; abs braced, glutes engaged; re-engage lats if shoulders hurt
weighted stretch for forearms, lats and arms; spinal decompression; shoulder relief
